overlap_risks: Classical finite-horizon truncation pathology (the well-known 'cliff-fall' effect where finite-horizon optimal control defers costs beyond step H).
Missing terminal value function / terminal set constraint (Lyapunov/viability kernel failure well documented since 1980s MPC literature).
Direct relabeling of rejected 'TD-MPC2 period-5 horizon-shadowing' and 'hard-boundary stiffness' via physical metaphors ('irreversible transition energy', 'boundary residual').
Conflation of environment irreversibility (dynamics reachability boundary) with world-model-specific vulnerabilities.
minimum_gate: Demonstrate that the failure is uniquely driven by a latent generative world-model vulnerability rather than baseline MPC myopic control: specifically, execute a true environment model (analytical dynamics) under identical horizon H and show that HD-ET *only* occurs in the learned world model under nominal Q/value estimates while the ground-truth model avoids the trap, without relying on task-level terminal cost absence.
repair: Strip the generic physical terminology ('energy trapping') and formalize it as a latent-space value estimation divergence specific to world-model representations: a model-based adversarial blind-spot where the latent transition model preserves local predictive fidelity while shifting the latent distribution into a deficient terminal value region that the critic fails to penalize. Include explicit control proofs eliminating standard finite-horizon terminal cost truncation.
falsifiers: Ground-truth dynamics MPC with horizon H experiences the identical post-horizon drop/irreversible state transition (proves it is classical horizon truncation, not a world model phenomenon).
Adding an accurate learned terminal value function V(s_{t+H}) removes the failure mode without modifying the transition model (confirms missing terminal cost).
Metric of 'residual energy' is linearly correlated with standard cumulative rollout divergence or known boundary OOD shifts across test seeds.
